hints: Focus on what raising pH really means, you need to make the soil less acidic by adding something basic or alkaline.
Look at each formula and ask which one can actually supply hydroxide ions, $\text{OH}^-$, to neutralise soil acidity.
Remember that ammonium salts tend to make soil more acidic, while a metal hydroxide will neutralise $\text{H}^+$ and push the pH up.
walkthrough:
**Understand the goal**

Raising pH from 5.5 to above 6.0 means decreasing acidity. You need to remove $\text{H}^+$ from the soil.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{acid + base} \rightarrow \text{salt + water}$$

**Check for a base**

A compound that provides $\text{OH}^-$ ions will neutralise $\text{H}^+$ ions:
$$\text{H}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is a base and dissociates to give hydroxide:
$$\text{Ca(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+} + 2\text{OH}^-$$

**Reject the acidic and neutral salts**

Ammonium ions act as acids in soil, releasing $\text{H}^+$:
$$\text{NH}_4^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+$$
So $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ lower pH, not raise it. $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ is a neutral salt and has no neutralising effect. Only the hydroxide raises pH.

options.A: Incorrect. $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ is an acidic fertiliser. The $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion releases $\text{H}^+$ in soil, which would lower pH further, the opposite of what is needed.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ also contains $\text{NH}_4^+$ which acts as an acid and increases $\text{H}^+$ concentration. It is used to lower pH or supply nitrogen, not to neutralise acidity.
options.C: Correct. $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, slaked lime, is a base. It provides $\text{OH}^-$ ions that neutralise $\text{H}^+$ in acidic soil to form water, so the pH rises from 5.5 to above 6.0. This is the standard liming process.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ is formed from a strong acid and strong base, so it is approximately neutral in solution. It supplies calcium and nitrate as fertiliser but provides no $\text{OH}^-$ to neutralise acidity.
